newsitem.title: USA: Jerry Garcia ex-wife wins $5 mln claim against estate.
newsitem.headline: Jerry Garcia ex-wife wins $5 mln claim against estate.

text.p: A judge ruled on Wednesday that the estate of Grateful Dead guitarist Jerry Garcia must honour a $5 million divorce agreement the musician made with his second wife, her lawyer said.
Family court judge Michael Dufficy ruled in favour of ex-wife Carolyn "Mountain Girl" Garcia, who sued the estate in family court in San Rafael near San Francisco.
The judge upheld the divorce agreement as valid and enforceable, Carolyn's lawyer, David Phillips, said.
Phillips said Carolyn had been paid $400,000 by the artist before his death and that the estate now owed her $4.6 million. "Now we just have to make sure the money is paid," he added.

Phillips said the decision meant Deborah Koons Garcia, the guitarist's third and last wife and the co-executor of his estate, would have to pay Carolyn from the estate about $250,000 a year for the next 18 years.

Paul Camera, an attorney for the estate, said he would ask the judge to reconsider the decision. "If he doesn't change his mind, I've already told my client that she has a legitimate appeal," he said.

Carolyn and Jerry Garcia were married in 1981. They separated in 1990 and were divorced in January 1994, Camera said. He has described their marriage as a sham and said that drugs had impaired the judgment of the guitarist.
Jerry Garcia married Deborah Koons in February 1994.

The guitarist died of a heart attack in August 1995 while at a northern California drug treatment centre. After his death, his estate stopped making the payments to Carolyn and disputed her right to the funds, Camera said.
Her claim was one of several multi-million dollar claims that have been filed against the estate following the guitarist's death.
